title: Scan for fused words
statement: Scan generated student-facing text for fused words such as 'themain' or 'tothe', and fail it when one appears, because early readers may not recognise them as words.
example: One rubric sets the whole diction score to 0.0 if a single merged non-word appears anywhere in the student-facing text.
detail: The AP work's evaluator lists merged non-word forms such as 'themain', 'tothe' and 'inthe' as serious errors in its article and nonfiction-reading rubrics, especially for early-grade content where students may not recognise malformed words (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/prompts/article/evaluation.txt`, `icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/prompts/nonfiction_reading/evaluation.txt`). The article rubric sets the whole diction score to 0.0 if one appears anywhere in the student-facing text. The base and closed-ended question rubrics flag them too (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/_base_evaluation.txt`, `icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/closed_ended_evaluation.txt`), so four rubrics carry the rule.

evidence.quote: - **Merged non-word forms** in student-facing text: `themain`, `forclosure`, `becausethe`, `tothe`, `ofthe`, `inthe`, `sentenceending`, etc. - These are serious errors, especially for early-grade content where students may not recognize malformed words - If merged non-words appear ANYWHERE in the student-facing text, set `diction_and_sentence_structure = 0.0`
